title: fullcast state
description: Documentation reference for .fullcast/state.json — not enforced by a script (architecture.md §5: reading/editing this file is model work via Read/Edit, not script work). Read this before hand-editing the file. state.json is the single source of truth; .fullcast/report.md is a rendering of it, never a second source (architecture.md §13).

context_project.description: Pointer to context_project.md at the project root (architecture.md §11) — the file itself lives OUTSIDE .fullcast/ because it serves any methodology, not just fullcast.

artifacts.description: DEPRECATED since architecture.md v13 — a project can now hold several concurrent initiatives, so a single project-level brief/prd no longer makes sense. Superseded by initiatives[].artifacts. Kept only so pre-v13 projects don't fail validation; new projects should have this empty/absent.

initiatives.description: The grouping level above features (architecture.md §21) — 'a bigger demand that has features that have tasks', in the project owner's own words. One PRD cycle = one initiative by default.

id.description: I01, I02, ... Zero-padded, sequential, no gaps, global across the project (same rule as feature id). Folder: .fullcast/<id>-<kebab-name>/.

status.description: in_progress: at least one feature not yet done. features_done: every feature_ids entry is stage 'done', but changesfullcast hasn't been generated yet (the human said 'not now' when evaluator asked, architecture.md §21). archived: changesfullcast generated — this initiative is closed.

branch.description: Git branch this initiative's work happened on, if a dedicated one was created (architecture.md §21) — e.g. 'initiative/I01-cadastro-usuario'. null when the human declined the suggestion and stayed on whatever branch was current.

artifacts.description: Supersedes the deprecated project-level artifacts field — brief/prd now belong to the initiative that owns them.

feature_ids.description: Every feature this initiative owns. A feature's own initiative_id field must point back here — the two are kept in sync by whoever adds the feature (pm normally; tech-lead in the imported-PRD fallback, architecture.md §21).

changesfullcast.description: null until generated. Set by fullcast-changes (architecture.md §21).

status.description: pending_approval means drafted and saved to disk, awaiting the human checkpoint (architecture.md §15) before the next role may start. Only 'done' unlocks the next role.

id.description: F01, F02, ... Zero-padded, sequential, no gaps, global across the project (not reset per initiative). Next ID = read the array, take the highest, add 1 (no script — architecture.md §5).

initiative_id.description: The initiative this feature belongs to (architecture.md §21) — must also appear in that initiative's feature_ids. null only for features created before v13 that haven't been backfilled yet; every feature created from v13 on must set this.

methodology.description: Locked at feature creation. Immutable afterwards (architecture.md §9) — a feature is only ever closed by the methodology that opened it.

estimated_difficulty.description: Set by tech-lead in tasks.md generation.

real_difficulty.description: Set by evaluator at done, from what the task reports showed (deviations, retries). null until then (architecture.md §13).

tokens_estimated.description: Sum of per-task token estimates for this feature. Set at done. null until then.

fix_cycles.description: Incremented once per fullcast-developer-fix-runner run against this feature (architecture.md §19). Distinguishes original tasks.md tasks from post-rejection corrective passes — never folded into the tasks[] list.

id.description: <feature-id>-T<n>. Includes the feature id because tasks live in a flat list, unlike contract.md items which are always read within their own feature's file.

phase.description: The tasks.md phase this task belongs to (Phase 1, 2, 3...), set by tech-lead. This list is flat for lookup, but phase must stay visible here and in every developer task report — otherwise the grouping tech-lead defined disappears the moment developer starts executing (found by a user reading the wordcount example and losing track of which task belonged to which phase).
